blocks.transcript:
1. Introduction to Gemini in Google Docs
Hello and welcome to Gemini in Google Docs, a course in our Google Workspace with Gemini series.

This course introduces you to the specific Docs features included in Google Workspace with Gemini.

You learn how to use Gemini in Docs to write new text, or refine existing text.

You also explore how to use proofread to check your grammar and spelling or get stylistic suggestions.

You then complete a hands-on activity acting as a sales representative for Cymbal Retail, writing a blog post about the new product.

Gemini in Google Docs uses generative AI to help you work more efficiently.

Remember, generative AI tools, including Gemini, might suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information.

Don't rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial, or other professional advice.

It's also important to remember that the Gemini feature suggestions don't represent Google's views, and should not be attributed to Google.

You might find that some features aren't available in your Google Workspace edition or other features might be restricted by administrative policies.

If you have questions, contact your Google Workspace Administrator.

blocks.transcript:
1. Create Content with Gemini
You can access Gemini in Docs by opening a Google Docs document on your desktop.

If you haven't already, visit docs.google.com in your browser.

To edit an existing Google Docs document, select the document.

To create a new document, select the Blank template in the template gallery.

You can also create a new document by typing docs.new into your desktop browser.

In this lesson, you learn how to use the "Help me write" feature to create text-based content.

When you open a new document, you may be prompted with multiple options to quickly get started writing.

Select Help me write.

If you're working on an existing document, you can access the Help me write prompt options from the left margin of your document.

A text input will open where you can enter your prompt.

Suppose you work in marketing for the athletic footwear division and would like some inspiration for an upcoming social campaign.

You can use "Help me write" in Docs to help you brainstorm a captivating tagline or draft social media posts by providing

a prompt like: "Generate 3 social media posts that highlight the benefits of our athletic shoes with a focus on comfort and performance."

If you work in sales, you can use Gemini to help you prepare for a meeting with a high-profile client.

For example, you can ask Gemini to write 5 thoughtful questions to ask a VP of Merchandising about their strategy for the upcoming year.

Or maybe you're in human resources and want to revamp the new employee onboarding experience for financial analysts.

Ask Gemini to create an onboarding checklist for the Finance team to quickly develop an important part of the new training program.

If you're in customer support, consider asking Gemini to summarize a transcript saved as a Google Docs document.

Gemini can help you quickly summarize the troubleshooting steps already taken and provide a bulleted list of action items.

After you type your prompt, click Create.

You might need to wait a few moments for Gemini to generate a response.

If you like what's suggested, click Insert to add it to your document.

If you want to improve the generated response, you can choose to refine the generated text or update the prompt you provided.

You learn more about refining generated responses in the next lesson.

blocks.transcript:
1. Edit Prompts and Refine Text
In this demo, you explore how you can use Gemini in Docs to quickly brainstorm new ideas and draft documents.

You learn how to edit a prompt, and refine generated text.

Imagine you're an IT employee at a company with a hybrid work environment.

You're interested in using Gemini to generate a list of frequently asked questions about technical problems that can arise when working from home.

First, create content by using Gemini in Docs.

Open a new Google Docs document, and select "Help me write."

Type the prompt.

You can choose something like: "Write an FAQ document about challenges working from home."

Then, click Create.

If you like the message, select Insert.

Otherwise, you can change the original prompt to help generate a new response that better meets your expectations.

The original prompt was "Write an FAQ document about challenges working from home."

Gemini created a list of broad concerns that are not specific to technical issues.

However, the goal was to help employees troubleshoot and resolve common technical issues.

Rewrite the prompt to clarify to provide Gemini with more context.

Click the "Refine with a prompt" input box, and type a new prompt.

Change the prompt to: "Write 10 frequently asked questions and answers about technology issues when working from home."

Then press Enter.

Notice how Gemini has created a more appropriate list.

You can fine-tune your prompts if the results don't meet your expectation or if you believe there's room for improvement.

At the top of the prompt box, use the arrow keys to move between your different prompts and results.

Insert the result that best matches your requirement.

Regardless of your role, it's important to provide a descriptive prompt to help Gemini understand what you're looking for.

To help Gemini to better understand your expectations, avoid using jargon or technical language.

Also, you can provide examples of the type of content you're looking for.

Next, refine a draft.

Gemini in Docs can refine text, including text that you already wrote or text that was previously created with "Help me write."

Select the draft text you want to refine.

In this example, select the entire document.

At the end of the selected text, select Refine.

To make specific changes, type an instruction in the "Modify with a prompt" input box and press Enter.

Alternatively, use the predefined refinement options.

If you want to change the word choice in something you already wrote, select Rephrase.

You can also use the Rephrase option to change the wording of text generated by Gemini that you've already inserted into your document.

If the text is too long, select Shorten to reduce the length of the existing text.

However, if you want to make the text more detailed, select Elaborate.

To change the tone of the text to be more appropriate for a formal audience, select More formal.

Select Shorten to reduce the amount of text in this draft.

Refinement options are also available from the prompt box.

In addition to the options already discussed, Gemini can make the draft more casual, create a

bulleted list, and generate a summary of the entire document or a section of the document.

If you want to generate a new draft based on the original prompt, select Retry.

Select Bulletize to generate a bullet list of the current draft.

Either replace the current draft with the bulleted list, or insert it after the current draft.

The bulleted list has been inserted after the original draft.

blocks.transcript:
1. Proofread Documents
You can use Proofread as your personal editor to ensure that your document is polished and professional before you share it with others.

Aside from grammar and spelling suggestions, Proofread evaluates your word choice, use of active voice, conciseness, and sentence structure.

To use Proofread, open the document you want to review and click Proofread this document in the toolbar.

You can also access Proofread from the tools menu.

After the panel is open, you can review each suggestion and decide whether you want to approve or reject it.

To approve a change, select Accept suggestion.

To reject it, select Dismiss suggestion.

If you want to focus on one area of improvement at a time, you can filter suggestions according to the issue category.

To manage what Proofread checks for, open the proofread settings menu.

By default, all checks are enabled, but you can choose to clear any options that you want.

Note: If you change your Proofread settings, those updates apply to all of your documents.

After you have finished reviewing the suggestions, you can click the Close button to exit the panel.

Even if the panel is closed, Proofread continues working in the background.

If issues in your writing are detected, the icon will include a blue dot to indicate that proofread suggestions are available.

question.en:
You are working on a new product launch for an organic green juice named Cymbal Green. You have conducted market research and have a good understanding of consumer needs and preferences. You want to use Gemini to develop compelling product descriptions that convey the benefits of the new beverage.

Which of the following is the best prompt?
question.fr:
You are working on a new product launch for an organic green juice named Cymbal Green. You have conducted market research and have a good understanding of consumer needs and preferences. You want to use Gemini to develop compelling product descriptions that convey the benefits of the new beverage.

Which of the following is the best prompt?

text.en: Generate product descriptions that appeal to active individuals who seek a natural and effective energy boost.
text.fr: Generate product descriptions that appeal to active individuals who seek a natural and effective energy boost.

text.en: Create a product description for Cymbal Green that resonates with consumers seeking a convenient and portable way to stay energized throughout the day.
text.fr: Create a product description for Cymbal Green that resonates with consumers seeking a convenient and portable way to stay energized throughout the day.

text.en: Craft a product description for a new organic green juice called Cymbal Green that highlights the juice’s ability to boost energy levels and enhance performance.
text.fr: Craft a product description for a new organic green juice called Cymbal Green that highlights the juice’s ability to boost energy levels and enhance performance.

text.en: Write a product description for a new organic green juice called Cymbal Green.
text.fr: Write a product description for a new organic green juice called Cymbal Green.

explanation.en: This answer is correct. This prompt provides clear direction to the AI, and specifies the product's key attributes and the desired tone of the descriptions.
explanation.fr: This answer is correct. This prompt provides clear direction to the AI, and specifies the product's key attributes and the desired tone of the descriptions.

hint.en:
Specificity matters: the best prompt should name the product, describe what it is, AND state the key benefits you want emphasized

Compare prompts that include concrete details (product name + category + benefits) against those missing crucial information like what the product actually is

Strong prompts guide the AI toward your research findings by specifying desired attributes rather than leaving it to generate generic descriptions

question.en: You are a financial analyst at a bank and you are writing a report on economic trends. You want to ensure that the report is polished, so you decide to use Gemini's Proofread feature. Which of the following is a suggestion that Proofread might make to improve your report?
question.fr: You are a financial analyst at a bank and you are writing a report on economic trends. You want to ensure that the report is polished, so you decide to use Gemini's Proofread feature. Which of the following is a suggestion that Proofread might make to improve your report?

explanation.en: This answer is correct. Proofread can help you identify passive voice and suggest ways to make your writing more active.
explanation.fr: This answer is correct. Proofread can help you identify passive voice and suggest ways to make your writing more active.

hint.en:
Proofread focuses on writing quality improvements like clarity, tone, and grammar—think about which suggestion relates to making sentences more direct and impactful

Consider what a professional banking report needs: formal tone, conciseness, and clarity—which option aligns with strengthening sentence structure rather than changing word count or adding terminology?

Passive voice (like "The report was written") weakens professional writing; active voice ("I wrote the report") is a common writing improvement tool
